paper.title_en: Low-frequency Radio Observation of the Dark PeVatron LHAASO J2108+5157 Using uGMRT. II
paper.abstract_en: We present deep radio observations of the PeVatron candidate LHAASO J2108+5157 using the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT). Our observations reveal a persistent double-lobed radio source (GMRT$_{ext}$) within the vicinity of the ≥100 TeV γ-ray emission region, with consistent morphology across 400 MHz, 650 MHz, and 1.2 GHz. No alternative particle accelerators, such as supernova remnants or pulsar wind nebulae, are identified in the region, making GMRT$_{ext}$ the most plausible counterpart candidate. We measure the flux and spatially resolved spectra of the source using multiband radio data. The morphology remains stable across all bands, while a comparison of noncontemporaneous observations suggests possible flux variability. From the measured spectra of the lobes, the inclination angle of the jet is estimated to be 86 . ,° , 57 ± 1 . ,° , 15. The multiwavelength spectral energy distribution is modeled reasonably well with a leptohadronic scenario.
